forward_secrecy.conditions: Claimed in the CK model when the responder static secret is later revealed but the test-session initiator ephemeral secret sk_e was not exposed during the session.

protocol_characteristics.key_confirmation: Implicit only; no separate explicit key-confirmation message is specified.
protocol_characteristics.identity_binding: The certified responder public key pk_B is included in T; the submission claims resistance to identity misbinding and UKS patterns.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: Two-pass KEMTLS-PDK-style unilateral AKE using the same CCA-secure DKEM for static and ephemeral contributions.

components.name: M1
components.semantics: Fresh initiator ephemeral DKEM public key.

components.name: ct_S
components.semantics: DKEM ciphertext encapsulated to responder long-term pk_B, yielding static contribution ss_s.

protocol_flow.semantics: m1 = M1 || ct_S; initiator retains sk_e, ss_s and m1 as session state.

components.name: M2
components.semantics: DKEM ciphertext encapsulated to initiator ephemeral M1, yielding ephemeral contribution ss_e.

protocol_flow.semantics: Responder decapsulates ct_S with sk_B, computes transcript T, and returns m2 = M2.

key_schedule.transcript_hash: T = H(LABEL || pk_B || m1 || m2; N)
key_schedule.ephemeral_secret_erasure: The protocol figure directs the initiator to erase sk_e and m1 after deriving the session key; intermediate ephemeral computations should also be erased.

common_parameters.hash_xof_kdf: SM3-256 for ADKEX-128/256; SM3-based pseudo-XOF truncated to 512 bits for ADKEX-512

correctness.relationship: The session uses two correctness-relevant DKEM pairs, so Pr[session failure] <= 2*delta by a union bound.

security_claims.claim: Unilateral authentication of the responder through the certified long-term DKEM key.
Security in the Canetti-Krawczyk model with weak perfect forward secrecy.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Subject to proof assumptions and exposure restrictions

security_claims.claim: Session-key indistinguishability reduces to IND-CCA DKEM and random-oracle KDF assumptions.
Transcript and certified-key binding are claimed to prevent key misbinding/UKS and mitigate re-encapsulation attacks.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Even though DKEM has no independent key-binding guarantee

claimed_advantages.claim: Combines static and ephemeral DKEM contributions with transcript binding and claims CK-model wPFS.
A modular two-pass design using DKEM, a transcript hash, and a KDF.
Module-LWE arithmetic and interfaces align with the modern ML-KEM ecosystem and standardization evaluation.
Portable, AVX2, AArch64 NEON, and Cortex-M4 implementations are supplied with unchanged wire format.

limitations_and_constraints.description: Only the responder is authenticated; the initiator has no long-term authentication key.
The responder's certified long-term public key pk_B must be pre-distributed or otherwise authenticated.
The wPFS claim requires the test-session initiator ephemeral secret key not to have been exposed during the session.
Reconciliation gives nonzero failure; a session has two failure opportunities and is bounded by 2*delta.
Security relies on the submitted DKEM primitive, IND-CCA assumptions, and a random-oracle treatment of the KDF.
DKEM provides no independent key-binding guarantee; the AKE layer compensates by hashing pk_B and both messages into T.
Reported reference benchmarks use one Intel Core i9-10885H under Ubuntu 24.04/WSL2 and average 128 exchanges.
